description:
Station Yard Inc.: luxury crewed Stations for discerning captains.

Pick a ship from your fleet, then build or upgrade a Station in each of its slots.

Download v0.2.0 (beta)
Source code on GitHub | All releases

Requires: Starsector 0.98a. No other mods needed.

Save compatibility

Can be added to an ongoing game: yes.
Can be removed: no. Ships with Stations carry the Crew Stations hullmod, and a save that has them needs the mod to load. Keep a backup.
Other mods: compatible. Works with modded ships and modded heavy industries. Tested with Nexerelin, Exotica Technologies and Random Assortment of Things.

A message from Station Yard Inc.
Tired of crews who merely survive? Station Yard Inc., the Sector's most exclusive outfitter, fits your ships with hand-crafted crewed Stations: shield control rooms, engine rooms, missile magazines and more, staffed by the finest specialists money can rent. Visit any of our showrooms, conveniently located wherever there is heavy industry. Prices are high because quality is high. Also because we can.
Station Yard Inc. is not responsible for crew lost to vacuum, pirates or the Domain. Warranty void if boarded. Financing not available in your sector.

What the mod actually does
Dock at any market with heavy industry and visit the Station Yard Inc. showroom. There you can build dedicated, crewed compartments aboard your ships: a shield control room, an engine room, a missile magazine... Each Station improves one part of the ship and can be upgraded twice. They are expensive, they need extra crew, and they stay with the ship for good.

How it works

Find a Shipyard: any market with working Heavy Industry whose owner is not hostile, your own colonies included. The dock menu shows Visit the Station Yard Inc. showroom.
Pick a ship: frigates have 1 Station slot, destroyers 2, cruisers 3, capitals 4. Automated ships have no crew, so no Stations.
Order a Station from the Catalogue: ten types, each with its own requirement (shields, a phase cloak, fighter bays, the right weapon slot...).
Upgrade it: Standard, Deluxe, Platinum. Platinum needs a showroom with Orbital Works or a nanoforge.
Pay for it: credits plus heavy machinery, metals and rare metals, taken from your cargo, then your storage there, then the open market. Bigger hulls pay more.

Every Station level adds 10% to the ship's skeleton and max crew. A Station whose requirement is no longer met (shields turned into Shield Shunt, say) goes inactive: no bonus, crew still needed. Dismantling refunds 25% of the credits (the rest is a restocking fee, naturally).

The Catalogue: every Station, its effects at all three levels, and exactly where the materials will come from.

The ten Stations (level 1 / 2 / 3)
Shield Station (needs shields): shield damage taken -5/10/15%, turn and unfold rate +15/30/50%, upkeep -10/20/30%
Logistics Station: supplies per month -5/10/15%, fuel use -10/20/30%
Engine Station: top speed +5/10/15%, acceleration, deceleration and turn rate +15/30/50%
Energy Station (needs an energy slot): energy weapon damage +3/6/10%, energy flux cost -5/10/15%
Ballistic Station (needs a ballistic slot): rate of fire +5/10/15%, ballistic flux cost -5/10/15%
Missile Silo (needs a missile slot): missile ammo +25/50/100%, missile hitpoints +15/30/50%, reload rate +15/30/50%
Phase Station (needs a phase cloak): phase upkeep -10/20/30%, phase cooldown -10/20/30%
Reactor Station: flux capacity +5/10/15%, flux dissipation +5/10/15%
Damage Control Station: hull damage taken -5/10/15%, weapon and engine repairs +25/50/75%, crew lost -25/50/75%
Flight Deck (needs fighter bays): fighter replacement time -10/20/30%, fighter top speed +5/10/15%
Simulator Bay (reward, see below): max combat readiness +5/10/15, CR recovery +15/30/50%

The Crew Stations hullmod lists every Station and its crew cost in the refit screen.

Prices
For a destroyer. Frigates pay x0.5, cruisers x2, capitals x4 (credits and materials).
Level 1: 112,500 credits, 75 heavy machinery
Level 2: 300,000 credits, 150 heavy machinery, 375 metals
Level 3: 675,000 credits, 225 heavy machinery, 150 rare metals

A capital with four Platinum Stations is a late-game project on purpose. Station Yard Inc. thanks you for your business.

For proven customers only
Station Yard Inc. keeps some Stations for captains who have shown their worth. They show greyed in The Catalogue until you earn them:

Missile Silo: destroy an enemy capital ship.
Phase Station: hold 1,000,000 credits. Premium clients only.
Engine Station: carry 5,000 fuel. You clearly intend to go places.

Customer Relations will write to you when you qualify.

A reward for Descent veterans
Won a Run in Slay the Sector? Station Yard Inc. has heard, and adds the Simulator Bay to its Catalogue: as an exceptional pilot, you stream your combat exploits to boost crew morale. No one has to know it was a simulation. Any save, any faction, normal price. Neither mod needs the other.

This is a beta
Everything in the mod works, but it is still being polished:

Balance is a first pass. Some Stations may feel too strong or too weak, and prices too cheap or too expensive. Your feedback is exactly what will fix that.
Bugs are possible. Known: a ship sold to a market keeps its Stations if you buy it back.

Found a problem, or something felt off? Please tell me! The easiest way is the Report a problem page on GitHub: pick "Report a bug" or "Balance feedback", and a short form guides you (you only need a free GitHub account). Describe what happened in your own words. If you can, drag and drop the file starsector.log from your Starsector folder into the form: it helps a lot.
Replies in this thread are welcome too.

Every number (effects, slots, crew cost, prices, the level 3 rule) can also be changed in data/config/settings.json, if you like to tinker. With Console Commands installed, the crst command lists, adds and clears Stations.

Changelog
0.2.0 (beta)
Locked Stations: Missile Silo (destroy an enemy capital ship), Phase Station (hold 1,000,000 credits) and Engine Station (carry 5,000 fuel) are now earned, per save. Until then The Catalogue keeps their secrets. Customer Relations writes to you when you qualify. Stations you already built stay.
Simulator Bay: a new Station for winning a Run in Slay the Sector (that mod enabled).
Shorter tile statuses in The Catalogue; console crst unlock for testing.

0.1.1 (beta)
The shop is now run by Station Yard Inc., a luxurious megacorp: a showroom at every Shipyard, a slogan of the day, The Catalogue, signed orders and a restocking fee on returns.
Levels are now Standard, Deluxe and Platinum.

0.1.0 (beta)
First public release: ten Station types with three levels, Shipyards at heavy industry markets, the Station Yard Inc. showroom, the Crew Stations hullmod, and full configuration in settings.json.

Full history in the changelog.

Credits
Thanks to the people whose work and open source code taught me how Starsector mods are made, and whose mods I love playing:

wispborne, for the Starsector IntelliJ Template, TriOS, and everything they do for the modding community. I learned to make my first mod with their tutorials.
Lukas22041, for Second In Command and Random Assortment of Things, a great example of what a Starsector mod can be. I never play Starsector without Lukas's mods.
Histidine91, for Nexerelin, a reference for nearly every campaign question.
The Exotica Technologies authors, whose way of storing ship upgrades on the ship's variant this mod follows.
tracesfx, for the starsector-modding skill: the build, validation and log tools, and the API notes this project relies on.

And to Alex and the Fractal Softworks team for Starsector <3

Permissions: the mod is under the MIT license: use, change, fork or redistribute it freely, as long as the copyright notice and the license text stay with it.

AI use disclaimer
Some or all assets and code in this mod were created using AI tools:
Code: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), through Claude Code. It wrote most of the Java code, the build and art tooling, and the design and API documentation.
Code review: Claude was also used to review each milestone for bugs before release. No line of code reaches a release without a human review.
Art: the ten Station illustrations, the Crew Stations hullmod icon and the banner at the top of this post were made with Z-Image Turbo (Alibaba's Tongyi Lab), an open image model run locally in ComfyUI; the banner starts from the vanilla Onslaught sprite.

How it was made: I designed the mod (the Stations, the Shipyard rules, the screen and the balance) and directed every change. Each milestone was then played and tested in game by me, against a checklist, before it was merged. The full source and the design notes are public on GitHub.
